'''Robin Howard Lovell-Badge''' is a British [[developmental biology|developmental biologist]]. He is most well known for his discovery, along with [[Peter Goodfellow (geneticist)|Peter Goodfellow]], of the [[SRY gene]] on the Y-chromosome that is the determinant of sex in mammals.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Koopman|first1=Peter|last2=Gubbay|first2=John|last3=Vivian|first3=Nigel|last4=Goodfellow|first4=Peter|last5=Lovell-Badge|first5=Robin|title=Male development of chromosomally female mice transgenic for Sry|journal=Nature|year= 1991|volume=351|issue=6322|pages=117–121|doi=10.1038/351117a0|pmid=2030730|bibcode=1991Natur.351..117K|s2cid=3331979 }}</ref> They shared the 1995 [[Louis-Jeantet Prize for Medicine]]<ref>[https://www.jeantet.ch/en/prix-louis-jeantet/laureats/1995-en/doctor-robin-h-lovell-badge/ Louis-Jeantet Prize]</ref> for their discovery. He was awarded the 2010 Waddington Medal from the [[British Society for Developmental Biology]] and the 2022 Genetics Society Medal.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Waddington Medal |url=https://bsdb.org/awards/the-waddington-medal/ |access-date=2026-05-18 |website=BSDB - British Society for Developmental Biology |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>[https://genetics.org.uk/news/genetics-society-medal-2022-prof-robin-lovell-badge/ Genetics Society Medal]</ref>  He is currently a Senior Group Leader and Head of the Laboratory of Stem Cell Biology and Developmental Genetics at the [[Francis Crick Institute]] in Central London.<ref>{{cite web|title=Robin Lovell-Badge: Biography|url=http://www.crick.ac.uk/research/a-z-researchers/researchers-k-o/robin-lovell-badge/biography/|website=The Francis Crick Institute|date=12 February 2025 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117114257/https://royalsociety.org/people/robin-lovell-badge-11839/|archivedate=2015-11-17|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/robin-lovell-badge-11839/|title=Dr Robin Lovell-Badge FMedSci FRS|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London}} One or more of the preceding sentences incorporates text from the royalsociety.org website where: {{blockquote|“All text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]].” --{{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies |accessdate=2016-03-09 |url-status=bot: unknown |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150925220834/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |archivedate=September 25, 2015 }}}}</ref>
